tactiq-alternative.0: Tactiq became popular as a simple Chrome extension that captures live transcripts in Google Meet, Zoom and Microsoft Teams without a bot. Still a good tool, too. So why switch? People look for a Tactiq alternative when they hit the free plan's 10 transcripts a month, need meetings outside the browser, or want more done with the notes.
tactiq-alternative.1: Below are 7 options, each matched to a reason for switching.
tactiq-alternative.2: The most common reason is the free plan: 10 transcripts and 5 AI credits a month. Upgrading helps only partly. Pro removes the transcript cap for $8 per user per month billed yearly, yet still includes just 10 AI credits a month.
tactiq-alternative.6: Lynkk keeps the bot-free option Tactiq users like, through its Chrome extension and Mac app, and adds a bot for Zoom, Google Meet and Teams when you prefer hands-off recording. In-person conversations too.
tactiq-alternative.9: Fathom records unlimited calls with video and transcripts for free on Zoom, Google Meet and Teams, which suits anyone whose main complaint is Tactiq's 10-transcript cap. Premium: $16 a month billed yearly.
tactiq-alternative.10: Notta gives 1,800 minutes a month on Pro for $8.17 billed yearly, and supports file uploads as well as live meetings. Free? Each conversation caps at 3 minutes. Treat it as a trial. More in [Notta pricing](https://lynkk.ai/blog/notta-pricing).
tactiq-alternative.11: Fireflies joins calls as a bot, transcribes them and pushes notes into CRMs, with Pro at $10 per seat billed yearly. Prefer no bot? Its desktop app records system audio instead.
tactiq-alternative.12: Like Tactiq, Otter shows a live transcript during calls, but it does so through its own agent and apps, and the free plan gives 300 minutes a month with a 30-minute cap per conversation. Limits: see [Otter.ai alternatives](https://lynkk.ai/blog/otter-ai-alternatives).
tactiq-alternative.13: On an eligible Google Workspace edition, Gemini's "Take notes for me" writes notes into a Google Doc in the organizer's Drive. Limits: 8 languages, one per meeting. Setup is explained in our guide to [Google Meet transcripts](https://lynkk.ai/blog/google-meet-transcript).
tactiq-alternative.14: Read AI adds engagement and talk-time analytics to summaries. Free covers 5 meetings a month; Pro costs $15 billed yearly. Comparison: [Read AI alternatives](https://lynkk.ai/blog/read-ai-alternative).
tactiq-alternative.15: Tactiq is a Chrome extension that captures live transcripts in Google Meet, Zoom and Microsoft Teams without adding a bot to the call. How? By reading the meeting's captions in your browser, saving them as a transcript, and letting you run AI prompts on the text.
tactiq-alternative.17: Accuracy depends more on audio quality and language than on the brand. Otter, Fireflies, Fathom and Lynkk record the meeting audio directly and run their own speech recognition on all of it, while caption readers depend on the meeting platform's captions.
tactiq-alternative.18: To compare accuracy fairly, run 2 tools on the same 3 meetings and check 4 things: names of people and companies, numbers and dates, technical terms, and speaker labels. Those errors take the longest to fix. Hindi speakers, or a team that switches between Hindi and English? Test that case specifically. Many tools expect one language per meeting.
tactiq-alternative.20: Tactiq keeps transcripts in your account and offers advanced data retention and SAML SSO on Business ($29.17 billed yearly). One catch for IT: browser extensions need permission to read the meeting page. Many IT teams review them before approving.
tactiq-alternative.22: Tactiq vs Notta comes down to capture and limits. Tactiq captures live captions from your browser with no bot and gives unlimited transcripts on Pro ($8 billed yearly); Notta joins meetings and transcribes uploads, with 1,800 minutes a month on Pro ($8.17 billed yearly).
tactiq-alternative.23: Lightweight browser transcripts? Tactiq. Also transcribing recorded files? Notta.
tactiq-alternative.28: For Google Meet specifically, the best Tactiq alternatives are Google's own Take notes for me (if your Workspace edition includes it), Fathom (free unlimited recording) and Lynkk (Chrome extension or bot, plus tasks and Jira). All 3 get you past Tactiq's 10-transcript free limit, each in its own way.
tactiq-alternative.29: Need the recording too? See our guide on [how to record a Google Meet call](https://lynkk.ai/blog/record-google-meet-call).
tactiq-alternative.32: Lynkk is the best alternative if you want follow-up work done. Fathom wins for free unlimited recording, and Notta for cheap transcription minutes and file uploads. Fireflies suits CRM-driven teams, and Google Meet's built-in notes suit English-only Workspace teams.
tactiq-alternative.33: Yes. Tactiq's free plan includes 10 transcripts and 5 AI credits a month. For $8 per user per month billed yearly, Pro removes the transcript limit. Use AI summaries often? Unlimited AI credits start on the Team plan at $16.67 per user billed yearly.
tactiq-alternative.34: Tactiq is a widely used extension, and its Business plan adds SAML SSO and advanced data retention. Before installing, review the extension's permissions and your company's policy on browser extensions. Tell participants you are transcribing, too, since several US states require all parties to consent to recording.
tactiq-alternative.35: Tactiq's main competitors are Otter.ai, Fireflies.ai, Fathom, Notta, Read AI, Google Meet's built-in notes and Lynkk. Each takes its own approach to capture and follow-up. Compare them on free limits, price per user, and whether they also capture meetings outside the browser.
tactiq-alternative.36: Yes. Lynkk, Fathom, Fireflies, Otter and Read AI all work with Zoom and Microsoft Teams as well as Google Meet. Because bot-based tools join from your calendar, they keep working even when you are not running Chrome during the call. No browser needed.
tactiq-alternative.37: Yes, Lynkk supports Hindi and a Hinglish setting for mixed Hindi and English meetings. By contrast, Hindi is missing from the 8 languages Google Meet's Take notes for me supports. Before rolling any tool out, test it on a real 20-minute meeting in the languages your team uses.
